outcomes.text: Define accounting as the process of recording, analysing and reporting financial transactions.
Explain how accounting gives a structured framework for organising financial data.
Describe how accounting helps measure and monitor an entity's financial performance and health.
Define and explain terms such as assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, expenses, income, expenditure and capital.
Tell apart current and non-current assets and liabilities, and income statement versus balance sheet accounts.
Analyse business transactions using accounting terminology.
Prepare a statement of financial position for individuals and businesses.
Evaluate a business's financial position from assets, liabilities and owner's equity.
Interpret a business's financial position from its balance sheet.
Define financial, cost and management accounting.
Describe the information each branch of accounting provides.
Identify how information flows from financial accounting to cost and management accounting for decisions.

units.title: Domain B: Business transactions and Accounting Equation

outcomes.text: Define a sole proprietorship as a business owned and run by one person.
Define a partnership as a business shared by two or more owners.
Define a corporation as a legal entity separate from its shareholders.
State the accounting equation: assets equal liabilities plus owner's equity.
Identify and define assets as resources with future economic benefit.
Define liabilities as debts owed to outsiders.
Define owner's equity as the owners' residual stake after liabilities.
Use the balance idea: total assets always equal liabilities plus owner's equity.
Describe how transactions raise or lower assets, liabilities and owner's equity.
Illustrate common transactions and their effect on the accounting equation.
Solve for a missing element of the equation when two are given.
Define a financial transaction as an exchange involving assets, liabilities or owner's equity.
Classify transactions as revenue, expense, asset purchase, liability, or equity change.
Explain why accurate recording of transactions matters for reporting and decisions.

units.title: Domain C: Recording and Reporting Financial Transactions

outcomes.text: Describe the double-entry system of accounting.
Explain the purpose of double-entry accounting.
Identify accounts, debits, credits and the general ledger as its components.
Distinguish debits from credits.
Explain why transactions are journalised: to record them in order.
Describe the journal as the first step, a chronological record of activity.
Create journal entries for sales, purchases, expenses and cash transactions.
Explain the purpose of ledger accounts for each asset, liability, equity, revenue and expense.
Select the correct ledger accounts for posting journal entries.
Post journal entries to ledgers applying debit and credit rules.
Show how ledger accounts reflect both sides of each transaction.
Define a trial balance listing all ledger balances.
Explain that a trial balance checks accuracy by confirming debits equal credits.
Illustrate the trial balance format with account names and debit and credit columns.

units.title: Domain D: Adjusting Entries and Financial Statements

outcomes.text: Explain the purpose of adjusting entries.
Describe accruals and deferrals (prepaid expenses and unearned revenue).
Prepare adjusting entries for accrued revenue and expenses.
Make estimated adjustments such as depreciation and allowance for doubtful accounts.
Define an income statement showing revenue, expenses and net income or loss over a period.
Identify its components: revenues, expenses and net income or loss.
Explain why revenues and expenses are presented in a set order.
Define a balance sheet as a snapshot of financial position at a point in time.
Identify balance sheet components: current and non-current assets and liabilities, and owner's equity.
Describe the balance sheet format: assets, then liabilities and owner's equity.
Prepare a balance sheet from given financial data.

units.title: Domain E: Accounting for Subsidiary/Book, Banking Transactions, and Bills of Exchanges

outcomes.text: Describe subsidiary journals as specialised records for specific transaction types.
Identify cash, petty cash, purchase, sales, returns and bills books.
Explain the format and columns of each subsidiary book.
Record transactions in the proper subsidiary book.
Explain banking transactions such as deposits, withdrawals, cheques and electronic transfers.
Differentiate savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
Analyse bank statements to reconcile and find errors.
Describe a bill of exchange as a negotiable instrument.
Explain the drawer, drawee and payee.
Differentiate promissory notes and trade bills.
Apply the procedure for recording a bill of exchange.

units.title: Domain F: Accounting for Non-Profit Organization and Accounting for Incomplete Records

outcomes.text: Define non-profit organizations.
Differentiate for-profit and non-profit organizations with examples.
Express the terms and concepts used in non-profit accounting.
List the sources of funds of non-profit organizations.

topics.title: Benchmark II: Income and expenditure accounts

outcomes.text: Define the income and expenditure account.
Differentiate receipts and payments from income and expenditure.
Prepare income and expenditure accounts.
Prepare a non-profit organization's balance sheet.
Define accounting for incomplete records or single entry.
Differentiate single and double entry with examples.
Identify the limitations of the single entry system.
Define the statement of affairs and tell it apart from a balance sheet.
Calculate opening and closing capital.
Prepare profit and loss account and statement of affairs with adjustments.
Convert single entry records into double entry.

units.title: Domain G: Depreciation, its Nature, and Methods of Calculation

outcomes.text: Define plant assets.
Determine the cost of plant assets.
Distinguish capital from revenue expenditures.
Classify plant assets as tangible, intangible and natural resources.
Define depreciation.
Differentiate depreciation, depletion and amortization.
Compute cost and depreciable cost of fixed tangible assets.
Compute depreciation by straight-line and declining-balance methods.

units.title: Domain H: Accounting for Surplus, Reserves and Funds: Nature-types and creation, and Accounting for Consignments

topics.title: Benchmark I: Surplus, reserves and funds

outcomes.text: Define surplus, reserves and funds.
List types of reserves: general, specific and capital.
Differentiate capital reserve from revenue reserve.
Distinguish general, special revenue and endowment funds.
Define accounting for consignment arrangements.
Differentiate consignment from regular sales.
Identify the roles of consignor and consignee.
Interpret consignment terms, conditions and legal and financial aspects.
Define principles of revenue recognition in consignments.
Understand revenue is recognised only when the consignee sells to a third party.
Identify how unsold consignment goods are handled.
Explain that the consignor keeps ownership and unsold goods are not the consignee's expense or inventory.
Define a partnership business.
Classify partners as active, sleeping or nominal.
Describe the essential elements of a partnership.
Develop a partnership agreement setting out agreed terms.
Define formation of a partnership and merger of two sole proprietorships.
Identify the legal requirements and steps to register a partnership.
Calculate net worth and record journal entries on formation.
Prepare a partnership balance sheet.

topics.title: Benchmark III: Profit and loss distribution

outcomes.text: Define profit and loss in a partnership.
Determine profit and loss sharing ratios from the agreement.
Identify allocation of salaries, interest on capital and bonuses to partners.
Create partnership final accounts including profit and loss distribution.

topics.title: Benchmark IV: Admission of a new partner

outcomes.text: Express the conditions for admitting a new partner.
Differentiate capital from investment.
Prepare a balance sheet after admission of a new partner.
Compute a new partner's capital under bonus, goodwill or direct purchase of interest.

topics.title: Benchmark V: Retirement of a partner

outcomes.text: Define retirement in a partnership and its conditions.
Record retirement entries at par, bonus, goodwill or direct sale of interest.
Compute and record revaluation.
Prepare a revised balance sheet.

units.title: Domain J: Accounting for Joint Stock Companies

outcomes.text: Define a joint stock company and its characteristics.
Classify the different kinds of companies.
Explain the procedure of forming a company in overview.
Illustrate the memorandum of association, articles of association and prospectus.
Describe the different types of share capital.
Illustrate the modes of issuing shares and debentures.
Prepare entries for issuing shares at par, premium or discount.
Prepare entries for issuing and redeeming debentures.
Prepare a statement of appropriation of income and a corporation's financial statements.
